name: Mango Tree
area: Janata Plot, Hampi Bazaar, near Virupaksha Temple
signature_dish: South Indian vegetarian thali served on a banana leaf
why_it_matters: Hampi's most famous restaurant and a near-cult address for travellers. It originally sat under an actual mango tree on a riverside lane near the Tungabhadra, but UNESCO heritage protection led the district administration to demolish encroaching structures, and Mango Tree relocated into the Hampi Bazaar grid at Janata Plot, a parallel lane to the Virupaksha temple street. The vegetarian thali is the dish locals and repeat visitors send first-timers here for.
insider_tip: Order the full veg thali rather than a la carte — it is the dish the restaurant built its name on, and it is unlimited refills. Go before 1pm for lunch service when the thali batch is freshest; floor-cushion seating fills up at sunset. Pure-veg, no alcohol, cash and UPI both work.
signature_address: Janata Plot, near Virupaksha Temple, Hampi Bazaar, Hampi, Karnataka 583239

name: Laughing Buddha
area: Virupapura Gaddi (Hippie Island), Tungabhadra north bank
signature_dish: Paneer biryani eaten on river-facing floor mattresses
why_it_matters: The defining river-view café of Virupapura Gaddi, the boulder-and-paddy 'Hippie Island' across the Tungabhadra from Hampi Bazaar. Seating is on mattresses on the ground with what reviewers consistently call the best river view in all of Hampi. Ranked among the top restaurants in Hampi on Tripadvisor across 370-plus reviews — a backpacker fixture for sunset meals.
insider_tip: Reach the island by the coracle/ferry crossing from Hampi Bazaar before the boats stop in the evening, or by the long road bridge via Anegundi. Come for sunset — the river-facing mattresses are claimed early. Food is unhurried; order, then settle in.
signature_address: Virupapura Gaddi (Hippie Island), Hampi, Gangavathi Taluk, Karnataka 583231

name: Suresh Restaurant
area: Hampi Bazaar, inside Suresh Guest House, near Virupaksha Temple
why_it_matters: A budget bazaar institution tucked inside Suresh Guest House on the lively Hampi Bazaar strip, a favourite of Indian and international backpackers. It runs the classic Hampi traveller menu — South Indian, North Indian, Chinese and Israeli — but is singled out for generous portions, reasonable prices and a well-priced set breakfast. Tripadvisor 4.6/5.
insider_tip: The set breakfast is the value pick — toast, eggs, fruit, juice and chai for a backpacker price. Spinach soup and Dal Bukhara are the standouts beyond the breakfast spread. It is one of several near-identical bazaar menus, so go for the friendly service and portion size.
signature_address: Hampi Bazaar, near Virupaksha Temple, Hampi, Karnataka 583239

name: Mowgli's Cafe
area: Virupapura Gaddi (Hippie Island), Hampiriver Road, paddy-field side
signature_dish: Wood-fired pizza eaten in a paddy-field hut
why_it_matters: One of the oldest guesthouse-cafés on Virupapura Gaddi, the Hippie Island side of the Tungabhadra. The café sits among paddy fields and palm shade on Hampiriver Road, with the slow, hammock-and-cushion island rhythm. It is a long-running landmark on the island traveller circuit alongside Laughing Buddha.
insider_tip: It is set back from the river among the paddy — quieter than the riverfront cafés, good for an afternoon with a book. Reachable on the island after the coracle crossing from Hampi Bazaar. Order the pizza, which the kitchen is known for.
signature_address: Hampiriver Road, Virupapura Gaddi (Hippie Island), Hampi, Karnataka 583231

name: Funky Monkey Restaurant
area: Hampi Bazaar, above Netra Guest House, near Virupaksha Temple
signature_dish: Vegetarian thali on a rooftop overlooking Virupaksha Temple
why_it_matters: A rooftop restaurant above Netra Guest House in Hampi Bazaar, run by chef-owner Shiva Kumar, with views over the bazaar and the Virupaksha temple gopuram. It is a pure-veg kitchen that earns repeat praise for the thali and a la carte cooking, and is one of the better-regarded bazaar-side rooftops on Tripadvisor.
insider_tip: It is in Hampi Bazaar — on the rooftop above Netra Guest House — not on the island, so no ferry needed. The breeze on the roof and the temple view make it a good sunset stop. Staff let you linger for hours; the handmade momos are made to order.
signature_address: Above Netra Guest House, Hampi Bazaar, near Virupaksha Temple, Hampi, Karnataka 583239

name: Gouthami Restaurant
area: Virupapura Gaddi (Hippie Island), Tungabhadra north bank
signature_dish: German-bakery breakfast in a riverside garden
why_it_matters: A long-standing garden café at Gouthami Guest House on Virupapura Gaddi, paired with a small German-style bakery — part of the slow island breakfast circuit on the Hippie Island side of the river. Open-seating, shaded, with the boulder-and-paddy backdrop that defines the island.
insider_tip: The German bakery counter is the reason to come — strudel and baked goods you won't find on the standard Hampi traveller menu. Quieter than the riverfront cafés; good for a late, unhurried breakfast after the morning coracle crossing.
signature_address: Gouthami Guest House, Virupapura Gaddi (Hippie Island), Gangavathi Taluk, Hampi, Karnataka 583231
